title: Types
description: The built-in types and type forms you use to describe values in Chic.

sections.title: Built-in types
sections.html:
Chic is statically typed. Write a type after :, or use := to let the compiler infer it from the initializer.

TypeMeaning
i8, i16, i32, i64Signed integers, with 8, 16, 32, or 64 bits.
u8, u16, u32, u64Unsigned integers of the same widths.
byteAn unsigned 8-bit type, like u8.
f32, float32-bit floating-point numbers.
f64, double64-bit floating-point numbers.
boolA boolean value: true or false.
charAn 8-bit character value.
runeA 32-bit Unicode code point; string iteration yields runes.
stringA native UTF-8 pointer-and-length value.
cstringAn alias for ^char, used with C strings.
voidNo return value; also used in untyped pointers such as ^void.
TypeInfo, any, SourceLocationCompiler-provided structures for type metadata, type-erased values, and source locations.
Type names such as i32 and string are built-in identifiers. The Keywords page lists reserved words separately.

sections.title: Declaring values
sections.html:
count : i32 = 42       // explicit type
name := "Chic"         // inferred string
var index := 0         // mutable binding
BufferSize :: 4096      // compile-time constant

Bindings are constant by default. Add var when you need to assign a new value.

sections.title: Composed types
sections.html:
FormMeaning
^TA pointer to a value of type T.
[N]TAn array with fixed-size storage for N elements.
[?]TAn array whose length is inferred from its initializer.
[]TA non-owning view over contiguous elements.
[T, U]A tuple containing multiple values.
func(T) -> UA callable function type.
funcptr(T) -> UA raw, context-free function pointer for native ABI boundaries.
values : [3]i32 = {10, 20, 30}
view : []i32 = values[:]
pointer : ^i32 = &values[0]
text : string = "hello"
c_text : cstring = c"hello"

sections.title: User-defined types
sections.html:
Declare your own types with struct, enum, union, or raw_union. An alias gives an existing type another name.

alias UserId : i64

Point : struct {
    x : f32 = 0
    y : f32 = 0
}

title: Keywords
description: Reserved words in Chic, with a short explanation of what each one does.

sections.title: Reserved words
sections.html:
These spellings are recognized by Chic's lexer and cannot be used as ordinary identifiers. Keywords are case-sensitive.

Built-in type names such as i32, f64, and bool belong on the Types page.
KeywordRole
aliasGives an existing type another name.
breakExits an enclosing loop or switch.
caseIntroduces a branch in a switch.
castExplicitly converts a value to a specified type.
continueSkips to the next loop iteration.
defaultIntroduces the fallback branch of a switch.
deferSchedules an action for the end of the current scope.
elseIntroduces an alternative branch.
enumDeclares an enumeration type.
falseThe false boolean value.
forBegins a loop.
funcDeclares a function or a callable type.
funcptrDescribes a raw function pointer type.
ifBegins a conditional branch.
importImports a package.
inSeparates a loop binding from its sequence or range.
inlineEmbeds a structure's members in another structure.
letExplicitly declares a constant binding.
matchSelects a result through pattern matching.
newAllocates and initializes a value.
nullThe null pointer value.
or_defaultSupplies a fallback value for an error result.
or_elseA legacy synonym for or_default.
or_errorSubstitutes an error during error propagation.
raw_unionDeclares a union without a runtime tag.
releaseReleases an allocated value.
returnExits a function, optionally returning a value.
sizeofQueries a type's size.
stepSets the increment of a range loop.
structDeclares a structure containing named fields.
switchBranches on a value using cases.
trueThe true boolean value.
tryPropagates an error result to the caller.
typeofObtains runtime type metadata.
unionDeclares a tagged union.
varDeclares a mutable binding.

sections.title: Directives and attributes
sections.html:
Directives begin with #. Attributes begin with @ and annotate declarations.

SpellingRole
#if, #elif, #else, #endConditional compilation.
#packageDeclares a logical package.
#import_libDeclares a native library dependency.
@extensionMakes a function available through method-call syntax.
@internalRestricts a declaration to its package.

Attribute names such as extension are not reserved word keywords.

sections.title: Constants
sections.html:
Chic declares compile-time constants with ::.

MaxItems :: 128
PacketLimit : u16 :: 65_535

title: Structs
description: Group related values into a named type with fields and defaults.

sections.title: Declaration
sections.html:
Write the type name, a colon, and struct. Inside the body, each field has a name and a type, with an optional default value.

Point : struct {
    x : f32 = 0
    y : f32 = 0
}
PartMeaning
PointThe new structure's name.
: structDeclares a structure type.
x : f32A named field with an explicit type.
= 0The field's default initializer.

sections.title: Initialization and fields
sections.html:
Use Type { ... } to construct a value. Named field initializers begin with a dot. Use var if the value needs to change.

origin := Point {}
var point := Point { .x = 10, .y = 20 }

point.x = 30
horizontal := point.x

sections.title: Extension methods
sections.html:
Define an ordinary function with @extension. Its first parameter is the receiver. A pointer receiver lets the function update the original structure.

@extension
translate : func(self : ^Point, dx : f32, dy : f32) {
    self.x += dx
    self.y += dy
}

point.translate(2, -4)

sections.title: Generic structures
sections.html:
Add type parameters after struct, then supply concrete types when constructing a value.

Pair : struct<T, U> {
    first : T
    second : U
}

pair := Pair<i32, bool> { .first = 42, .second = true }

sections.title: Embedding
sections.html:
Use inline inside a structure to embed another structure and expose its fields directly.

This example uses the Point type declared above. NamedPoint embeds its x and y fields and adds a name field of its own.

NamedPoint : struct {
    inline Point
    name : string = ""
}

var point := NamedPoint { .x = 10, .y = 20, .name = "spawn" }

// Access the embedded fields directly.
point.x = 30
horizontal := point.x // 30
vertical := point.y   // 20
label := point.name   // "spawn"

inline Point lets you initialize the embedded fields with .x and .y, then read or update them with point.x and point.y. The name field belongs to NamedPoint.

title: Functions
description: Declare reusable behavior with typed parameters and return values.

sections.title: Declaration
sections.html:
Write the function name, : func, and a parameter list. An arrow introduces the return type.

add : func(a : i32, b : i32) -> i32 {
    return a + b
}

result := add(10, 20) // 30
PartMeaning
addThe function's name.
a : i32, b : i32Named, typed parameters.
-> i32The type returned to the caller.
return a + bComputes and returns the result.

sections.title: No return value
sections.html:
Omit the return type when the function performs an action without returning a value.

increment : func(value : ^i32) {
    ^value += 1
}

sections.title: Default arguments
sections.html:
Give a parameter a default with =. Parameters with defaults must come last. Arguments are passed by position.

add_with_default : func(a : i32, b : i32 = 10) -> i32 {
    return a + b
}

first := add_with_default(5)     // 15
second := add_with_default(5, 2) // 7

sections.title: Generic functions
sections.html:
Place type parameters after func. Chic can infer the type argument from a call and specializes the function at compile time.

max_of : func<T>(a : T, b : T) -> T {
    if a > b { return a }
    return b
}

largest := max_of(3, 7) // T is inferred
Generic parameters are unconstrained. Write <T>; constraint forms such as <T : i32> are not supported.

sections.title: Multiple return values
sections.html:
Return a tuple when a function needs to produce more than one value.

divide : func(a : i32, b : i32) -> [i32, i32] {
    return [a / b, a % b]
}
